about: The earnings-quality signals eq.py reads from supplied facts. Every text row carries its source: a siglia-fin-concepts row, a dated Research note or ruling, an ER-001 rubric row as Research ruled it on 26 Sep 2026, a CFR section read from the cached eCFR (as of 2026-09-24), FASB's 2026 taxonomy, or the Corpus pack. No signal carries a line: Research has not ruled on earnings-quality thresholds.

signals.title: Cash conversion: operating cash flow against net income

definition.text: Operating cash flow set against net income for the same fiscal year: a ratio when net income is above zero, the difference when it is zero or below. It is something to examine against the company's own history and a named peer set, not a line.

formula.text: operating cash flow / net income, same period; when net income is zero or below, the ratio is not given and operating cash flow minus net income is shown instead.

inputs.text: Operating cash flow, total.
Operating cash flow from continuing operations; the discontinued part is a separate element.

Net income attributable to the parent (NetIncomeLoss) first, as Research's case-question readings (section 1) read it, then ProfitLoss, which includes noncontrolling interests, when NetIncomeLoss is absent; the element used is named. Operating cash flow is consolidated, so when ProfitLoss is held and differs, the difference, the noncontrolling interests' share, is shown.
inputs.source: siglia-fin-concepts CF-08 ; siglia-fin-concepts PG-02 ; Research 2026-09-24 case-question-readings §1 ; FASB US GAAP Taxonomy 2026 (siglia-xbrl-element) ; Research 2026-09-26 b2-skill-checks

inputs.text: Income from continuing operations: the consolidated figure, including the noncontrolling interests' portion, first, to match the consolidated continuing-operations cash flow; then IncomeLossFromContinuingOperations, which FASB labels attributable to the parent. When the parent-only figure is used, the line says so.
inputs.source: siglia-fin-concepts RF-40 ; siglia-fin-concepts CF-10 ; FASB US GAAP Taxonomy 2026 (siglia-xbrl-element) ; Research 2026-09-26 b2-skill-checks

period.text: Fiscal year or TTM; this skill reads fiscal-year durations only, each from its own start and end dates.

rules.text: Pair operating cash flow with an earnings figure on one perimeter: when discontinued operations are present and both continuing-operations figures are held, the continuing pair is used. Operating cash flow is consolidated, so a parent-only earnings figure beside it is named, and the noncontrolling interests' share is shown when the consolidated figure is held.
rules.source: siglia-fin-concepts CF-08 ; siglia-fin-concepts CF-10 ; Research 2026-09-26 b2-skill-checks

rules.text: A ratio calculated only from GAAP measures is not a non-GAAP financial measure.
When earnings are a loss in both years compared, the change is stated as the loss narrowed or widened, from both years' figures; never "improved".

pitfalls.text: Structural add-backs (depreciation, stock-based pay, impairments) lift the ratio above 1 without any change in what was earned in cash; compare within the company's history or a named industry.
A zero or negative net income flips or explodes the ratio, so the ratio is guarded.

A 10-Q statement of cash flows runs year-to-date (3, 6 or 9 months), so only a first-quarter figure is the quarter; a filer may also present a cumulative twelve months, and a single-crop agricultural registrant may give twelve-month statements instead. The duration is read from each fact's own dates.

not_applicable.text: Lender-type filers, as Research's section 11 tests decide them: operating cash flow mixes lending, deposit and trading flows, so the market does not read it for them (CF-08, CF-11).
not_applicable.source: siglia-fin-concepts CF-08 ; siglia-fin-concepts CF-11 ; Research 2026-09-24 case-question-readings §11

signals.title: Accruals: earnings not matched by operating cash, over average total assets

definition.text: The part of earnings that is not (yet) operating cash, scaled by the size of the balance sheet. Research since Sloan (1996) finds the accrual part of earnings persists less than the cash part.

formula.text: (earnings - operating cash flow) / the average of opening and closing total assets: the cash-flow method, preferred in later research (Hribar and Collins 2002) over Sloan's balance-sheet method.

inputs.text: Total assets at the opening and the closing balance-sheet dates of the fiscal year.

period.text: Annual (fiscal year), with average total assets across the year's opening and closing balance sheets.

rules.text: Sign: positive accruals mean earnings above operating cash flow.
Earnings and operating cash flow are paired as for cash conversion: the continuing-operations pair when discontinued operations are present and both are held.
No authoritative line makes accruals high; the research ranks firms into deciles, so a builder ranks within a stated universe rather than drawing a cut-off.

pitfalls.text: Scale by average total assets, never the closing balance alone.
Large impairments push accruals far below zero without saying anything about cash collected.
The balance-sheet method is distorted by acquisitions, divestitures, FX and reclassifications; this skill uses the cash-flow method.

not_applicable.text: Lender-type filers, as Research's section 11 tests decide them: financial firms are excluded in the research designs (CF-10), banks and insurers have no meaningful current and non-current split (RF-40), and operating cash flow is not read for them (CF-08, CF-11).
not_applicable.source: siglia-fin-concepts CF-10 ; siglia-fin-concepts RF-40 ; siglia-fin-concepts CF-08 ; siglia-fin-concepts CF-11 ; Research 2026-09-24 case-question-readings §11

signals.title: Receivables growth against revenue growth, and days sales outstanding

definition.text: Receivables growth set against revenue growth over the same fiscal year, with days sales outstanding at both year ends. Receivables growing faster than revenue is what the market examines for looser credit terms, slower-paying customers or earlier revenue recognition.

formula.text: DSO = receivables / revenue x the days in the period. This skill uses the ending balance with fiscal-year revenue and the fiscal year's own day count, and says so; the textbook form averages opening and closing receivables.

inputs.text: Accounts receivable, net, current, then the register's fallbacks in order.
Revenue, then the register's fallbacks in order. us-gaap:SalesRevenueNet is absent from the 2026 taxonomy; it stays last only as a fallback for historical filings.
inputs.source: siglia-fin-concepts CF-17 ; siglia-fin-concepts PG-11 ; FASB US GAAP Taxonomy 2026 (siglia-xbrl-element)

inputs.text: Contract assets are separate unbilled amounts; say whether they are included. This skill shows them apart and leaves them out of DSO.

period.text: Fiscal-year revenue with the matching year-end balances; compare with the prior fiscal year.

rules.text: Year-over-year change = this year / last year - 1; a percentage change on a zero or negative base is not given.

One element per series: the same receivables element at both dates and the same revenue element in both years. Switching elements silently creates breaks, so a comparison across elements is refused and both elements are named.

When discontinued operations are present in either year, the revenue comparison is made only on the recast figures from one filing, and then this signal itself carries a perimeter note naming the discontinued-operations facts and saying the comparatives are the recast ones; otherwise it reads not compared.

pitfalls.text: Credit sales are not disclosed, so total revenue is used; this understates DSO for firms with cash sales.
ReceivablesNetCurrent can include non-trade receivables.
Factoring and securitisation remove receivables and lower DSO without faster collection.
Acquisitions near the year end add receivables without a full year of revenue.
Seasonality around the balance-sheet date.

not_applicable.text: Lender-type filers, as Research's section 11 tests decide them: their operating flows carry lending and trading, and their balance sheets are usually unclassified (CF-15).

signals.title: One-off items in reported results, and the margin with and without them

definition.text: The separately tagged restructuring, impairment and settlement lines of the fiscal year, each with its fact, and the fiscal years in which each appears. Reported GAAP results include them; any figure that removes them is an analyst's adjustment, labelled, and shown beside the GAAP figure, never instead of it.
definition.source: siglia-fin-concepts CF-23 ; siglia-fin-concepts RF-11 ; siglia-fin-concepts RF-12

formula.text: Operating margin = operating income / revenue, same period. Beside it, the margin excluding the lines the caller names as separately presented on the face of the income statement, each with its sign.

inputs.text: Restructuring charges, the combined restructuring and write-down line, and cash paid for restructuring.
Goodwill, long-lived and intangible asset impairments, and the impairment totals.
Cash paid for legal settlements, an identifiable one-off cash line where tagged.
Operating income; CostsAndExpenses and OperatingExpenses are expense totals and never substitute for it.

period.text: The fiscal year; recurrence is read across the fiscal years supplied.

rules.text: A margin that excludes amounts included in GAAP operating income has the shape of a non-GAAP financial measure; it is labelled as Siglia's arithmetic on the filed lines named, and shown beside the GAAP margin.

In filings, a non-GAAP performance measure may not be adjusted to remove an item as non-recurring when it is reasonably likely to recur within two years or a similar item occurred in the prior two years. That is the SEC's line for a filer's own measures, not a market line; this skill lists the years each item appears and applies no line.
Which lines are separately presented, and whether they sit inside operating income, is read from the face of the income statement, not from the element name; the caller names them with their sign.

For a bank, decided only by registrant type or a Call Report or FR Y-9C link and never by SIC alone, the operating margin is not given: bank revenue is net interest income plus noninterest income, as ER-001 X7 rules (S-X 9-04 gives the captions), which a Revenues fact does not hold. A depository-institution SIC (6011-6089) with neither supplied leaves the question open, so the margin is not given either and the line names what the facts lack; 6091 and 6099 are not deposit banking.

pitfalls.text: Filers tag impairments on different elements (goodwill alone, goodwill and intangibles together, or a total), so the lines are listed and never summed.
Serial restructurers' one-off charges recur; the years each line appears are shown.

No Item 2.06 8-K does not mean no impairment: an impairment concluded while preparing the next periodic report needs no 8-K when that report, filed on time, discloses it. Item 2.05 has no such instruction; it is triggered only when the registrant commits to a plan under which material charges will be incurred, so a plan whose charges are not material carries no 8-K.
Most one-off cash items are not on the face of the cash flow statement; they sit in the notes or MD&A.

signals.title: The company's non-GAAP measures and their reconciliation

definition.text: A non-GAAP financial measure is a numerical measure of historical or future performance, financial position or cash flows that excludes amounts included in, or includes amounts excluded from, the most directly comparable GAAP measure.

formula.text: gap = the company's measure - its GAAP comparator; relative gap = gap / |GAAP comparator|; the reconciling items as the company lists them, and the periods in which each recurs.

inputs.text: The company's consolidated non-GAAP measures are not presented in the financial statements or notes, so they are not among the statement facts; they sit in furnished 8-K exhibit text and MD&A, and the caller supplies them with the document they came from. A measure GAAP requires, such as the ASC 280 segment profit measure, is not a non-GAAP measure; it sits in the notes, is tagged, and may carry an "adjusted" name.
inputs.source: siglia-fin-concepts PG-04 ; 17 CFR 229.10(e)(1)(ii)(C) ; 17 CFR 229.10(e)(5) ; Corpus pack (next6_packs_clean.json, earnings-quality) ; Research 2026-09-26 b2-skill-checks

period.text: The same fiscal period for the measure and its GAAP comparator; the history of the gap over several years.

rules.text: A registrant, or a person acting on its behalf, that publicly discloses material information including a non-GAAP measure must present the most directly comparable GAAP measure and a reconciliation, quantitative for historical measures. The registrant is a Section 12 or 15(d) reporter, not an investment company registered under the Investment Company Act.

A measure made public orally, by webcast or similar means meets the reconciliation requirement when the reconciliation is on the registrant's website and its location is given in the same presentation. So when the documents supplied print no reconciliation, the line says so and names the website as a source not held, never a finding that none exists.

Report a company-defined measure only as the company's own, citing its reconciliation, never as the standard figure. This skill computes no adjusted figure of its own except the ex-item margin ER-001 T5 asks for, labelled Siglia's arithmetic and shown beside the GAAP margin.
rules.source: siglia-fin-concepts QF-45 ; ER-001 T5 (ruled 2026-09-26) ; siglia-fin-concepts CF-23

pitfalls.text: Definitions change over time; compare a company's measure only with its own same-definition history.
Earnings releases are furnished, not filed; they are still on EDGAR but carry different liability.
Street EPS compiled by data vendors may not equal the company's own adjusted EPS.

signals.title: Capex and the costs the filer capitalised

definition.text: Costs the filer capitalised rather than expensed, shown as figures: capex as its two named lines (purchases of property, plant and equipment, and capitalised software), capitalised interest, and the gap between stock-based pay added back in operating cash flow and stock-based pay expensed. The cash paid for capex and for capitalised interest sits in investing, outside operating cash flow (CF-12; CF-04; FASB's 2026 documentation of InterestPaidCapitalized; ASC 230-10-45-13(c), by reference).
definition.source: Research ruling 2026-09-26 (capex and free cash flow) ; Research 2026-09-26 rubric-rows-ruled ; siglia-fin-concepts CF-12 ; siglia-fin-concepts CF-04 ; siglia-fin-concepts CF-22 ; FASB US GAAP Taxonomy 2026 (siglia-xbrl-element)

formula.text: capex = PP&E purchases + capitalised software, or PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets alone when held (it replaces the parts); capitalised software = PaymentsForSoftware (the total) when held, else PaymentsToDevelopSoftware + PaymentsToAcquireSoftware; capitalised software's share of capex = software / capex; the stock-based pay gap = the cash-flow add-back - the expense, same period.
formula.source: Research ruling 2026-09-26 (capex and free cash flow) ; Research 2026-09-26 rubric-rows-ruled ; Research 2026-09-26 b2-skill-checks ; siglia-fin-concepts CF-22

inputs.text: Purchases of property, plant and equipment, the first named capex line.
inputs.source: Research ruling 2026-09-26 (capex and free cash flow) ; Research 2026-09-26 rubric-rows-ruled ; siglia-fin-concepts CF-12

inputs.text: Capitalised internal-use software, the second named capex line, read first from PaymentsForSoftware: FASB defines it as cash paid for the development, modification or acquisition of internal-use software that qualifies for capitalization, a total. When it is held it is the software line, and the software parts held sit inside it and are never added to it.
inputs.source: Research ruling 2026-09-26 (capex and free cash flow) ; Research 2026-09-26 rubric-rows-ruled ; Research 2026-09-26 b2-skill-checks ; siglia-fin-concepts CF-12 ; FASB US GAAP Taxonomy 2026 (siglia-xbrl-element)

inputs.text: When PaymentsForSoftware is not held, capitalised software is PaymentsToDevelopSoftware (development or modification) plus PaymentsToAcquireSoftware (acquisition from vendors), both for internal use, each named.
inputs.source: Research ruling 2026-09-26 (capex and free cash flow) ; Research 2026-09-26 b2-skill-checks ; FASB US GAAP Taxonomy 2026 (siglia-xbrl-element)

inputs.text: A filer's investing line for capitalised software to be sold (ASC 985-20), which the capex ruling adds to capitalised software when tagged, is a filer extension or a line the caller reads from the filing. This skill does not read it and says so, so the capex it shows leaves that line out.
inputs.source: Research ruling 2026-09-26 (capex and free cash flow) ; Research 2026-09-26 rubric-rows-ruled

inputs.text: Purchases of PP&E, software and other intangible assets in one figure; when held it is the capex figure and replaces the parts.
inputs.source: Research ruling 2026-09-26 (capex and free cash flow) ; Research 2026-09-26 rubric-rows-ruled ; siglia-fin-concepts CF-12 ; FASB US GAAP Taxonomy 2026 (siglia-xbrl-element)

inputs.text: Capitalised interest; the capitalised interest paid sits inside capex, not operating cash flow.
Stock-based pay added back in the cash flow statement.
Stock-based pay expensed in the income statement.

rules.text: Capex is two named lines, PP&E purchases and capitalised software, added only when one of each is held. Capitalised software is PaymentsForSoftware when held, with the other software lines inside it and never added; else PaymentsToDevelopSoftware plus PaymentsToAcquireSoftware, each named. PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets replaces the parts and is never added to them. Free cash flow built on it is non-GAAP, and this skill does not compute it.
rules.source: Research ruling 2026-09-26 (capex and free cash flow) ; Research 2026-09-26 rubric-rows-ruled ; Research 2026-09-26 b2-skill-checks ; siglia-fin-concepts CF-12

rules.text: The add-back and the expense can differ when stock-based pay is capitalised, for liability-classified awards, or with discontinued operations; the gap is shown and no single cause is asserted.

pitfalls.text: Contract costs capitalised under ASC 340-40 (such as sales commissions) have no register row; they read not in the register.
us-gaap:CapitalizedComputerSoftwareNet is software to be sold, leased or marketed, and excludes internal-use software, so it is not the internal-use software balance.

PaymentsForSoftware is a total (development, modification or acquisition), and PaymentsToDevelopSoftware and PaymentsToAcquireSoftware are its parts. Adding the total to a part counts the software twice, so the total is taken whenever it is held and the parts held beside it are named and never added.
pitfalls.source: FASB US GAAP Taxonomy 2026 (siglia-xbrl-element) ; Research 2026-09-26 b2-skill-checks ; Research ruling 2026-09-26 (capex and free cash flow) ; Research 2026-09-26 rubric-rows-ruled

signals.title: Stock-based pay as a share of operating cash flow and revenue

definition.text: Stock-based pay is an expense paid in shares, so operating cash flow adds it back; part of reported operating cash flow exists because employees were paid in stock.

formula.text: stock-based pay / operating cash flow; stock-based pay / revenue.

inputs.text: The cash-flow add-back, then the expense; the element used is named.

period.text: The latest fiscal year or TTM; this skill reads the fiscal year.

rules.text: A ratio on a zero or negative base is not given; the two figures are shown instead.

For a lender-type filer the share of operating cash flow is not given, as operating cash flow is not read for it; for a bank the share of revenue is not given either, as bank revenue is net interest income plus noninterest income (ER-001 X7; S-X 9-04 gives the captions). A depository-institution SIC alone leaves the bank question open, and the share of revenue is not given then either, the line naming what the facts lack.
rules.source: ER-001 X7 (ruled 2026-09-26) ; siglia-fin-concepts CF-08 ; siglia-fin-concepts CF-11 ; 17 CFR 210.9-04 ; Research 2026-09-26 b2-skill-checks

pitfalls.text: Cash paid for shares withheld for employee taxes is real cash, but it sits in financing.

signals.title: Perimeter: discontinued operations and like-for-like comparisons

definition.text: Whether discontinued operations are present in a fiscal year compared, and how each comparison kept one perimeter: the continuing-operations pair when held, the recast comparative from the same filing, or no comparison.

formula.text: Present when an element of discontinued operations (their income or their operating cash flow) is held for the fiscal year with a value other than zero. A disposal group's revenue alone does not establish a discontinued operation, so it is named apart.
formula.source: siglia-fin-concepts PG-02 ; siglia-fin-concepts CF-08 ; Research 2026-09-26 b2-skill-checks

inputs.text: Income from discontinued operations and their operating cash flow.
inputs.source: siglia-fin-concepts PG-02 ; siglia-fin-concepts CF-08 ; siglia-fin-concepts PG-09

inputs.text: Revenue attributable to a disposal group, which FASB defines as including, but not limited to, a discontinued operation: it is named, and alone it never marks discontinued operations present.
inputs.source: FASB US GAAP Taxonomy 2026 (siglia-xbrl-element) ; Research 2026-09-26 b2-skill-checks

rules.text: When discontinued operations are present in either year, a year-over-year comparison uses figures from the same filing (the recast comparative, the latest filed being current), or it is not made.
When discontinued operations are present in either period, a revenue comparison carries a perimeter note naming them.

pitfalls.text: Discontinued operations can dominate a year's net income.
